description: Slack's hosted MCP server: search, messages, channels and canvases.

io.github.maxf98.streamdeck-mcp/studio.scopes: search:read.public search:read.private search:read.mpim search:read.im search:read.files search:read.users emoji:read channels:read groups:read im:read mpim:read chat:write channels:history groups:history mpim:history im:history channels:write groups:write im:write mpim:write reactions:read reactions:write canvases:read canvases:write users:read users:read.email files:read files:write lists:read lists:write
notes: Pre-registered OAuth app: Slack requires a client SECRET, so the code->token exchange runs on the registry service and `exchangeProxy` tells the Studio to route its redirect through it. The secret stays a Railway env var.

The client id is a literal here because this list is published as a static file. That is not a leak: a client id is public by construction (it rides in every authorize URL) and this exact value has been served unauthenticated from /registry all along.
The scopes are USER scopes (sent as user_scope in the authorize URL) because Slack's MCP server needs a user token (xoxp-), not a bot token (xoxb-).

The scopes are the full set Slack's MCP server uses (docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server, checked 2026-09-28) — its tool set is fixed, so any scope beyond this list unlocks nothing. The search:read.* variants replace the broad `search:read`, which needs Slack approval the app does not have.
